clue.text: Back again with golden girl for 18

indicators.note: going back means the joined words are to be read from the end to the start

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A golden girl returns for another round of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is IVANHOE; Rowena is the Saxon heroine of Scott's novel, so 'girl for 18' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is the heroine whom the knight marries in Walter Scott's historical novel.

clue.text: Churchman securing a supplier of energy

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes charge of some source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the plant that generates power for the electricity grid.

clue.text: 25 is a friend to women

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a friend to women.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is IDIOT. A wally is British slang for a silly, foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wally is informal British slang for a fool or a hopelessly inept person.

clue.text: Clubbing with Spooner's scalpel?

indicators.note: Spooner was the clergyman famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words

blocks.note: a scalpel is a light surgical knife; swap the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: A surgeon's blade is somehow paired with a night out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the L and N sounds of light knife gives night life.
explanation.definitionFit: Going clubbing means visiting bars and discos after dark, the entertainment of the town's evening scene.

clue.text: Musician who gives false accounts?

blocks.note: second meaning: a cheat who cooks the books

explanation.walkthrough: To fiddle the accounts is British slang for falsifying them, so a fiddler is both a violinist and a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays the fiddle, and someone who fiddles financial records is a fraudster.

clue.text: Saucy striker, perhaps

blocks.note: second meaning: an attacking player in football

explanation.surface: A cheeky centre-forward on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a striker as one example of an attacking player.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold, presumptuous person is called pushy; attacking footballers play up front in the advanced positions.

clue.text: Obligation to take turn in first performance

indicators.note: taking something in means absorbing it, so one word goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A performer is obliged to do their turn at a premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is an artist's opening appearance before the public, their initial show.

clue.text: "Power of Maths": record with which member secures unlikely hit

indicators.note: securing something means locking it inside, so one word holds the other
an unlikely version is an implausible rearrangement of the given letters

blocks.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A record titled 'Power of Maths' becomes a surprise hit for one band member.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the exponent to which a base must be raised, a power in mathematics.

clue.text: Live with faction pursuing heartless rogue

indicators.note: without a heart, the middle letters are removed and only the ends kept
pursuing means following behind, so the faction comes after

blocks.note: just the first and last letters
a side is a party or faction

explanation.surface: Someone lives among a gang chasing a callous villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there.

clue.text: Food past its sell-by date contains source of pandemic

indicators.note: containing something means holding it within, so one word wraps the other
the source is where something starts, so just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Out-of-date food harbours the origin of a worldwide disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic foodstuff eaten routinely, such as rice or bread.

clue.text: Everybody Russian keeps a model 13

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one word goes within the other

explanation.surface: Everyone in a Russian group keeps a model of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large crocodilian, a scaly cold-blooded animal of the class Reptilia.

clue.text: False turn in the toilets

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone takes a wrong turn into the lavatories.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake, counterfeit or sham.

clue.text: Meeting to vex proverbially patient character

blocks.note: to try someone's patience is to vex them
a saint, abbreviated; one proverbially has the patience of a saint

explanation.surface: A get-together designed to exasperate a famously patient person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic rendezvous between lovers.

clue.text: Drunk goes for pre-salted nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A tipsy person makes for the salted nuts at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the bar snack being eaten, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is informal slang for very intoxicated, blind drunk.

clue.text: Pig's head in cream - recipe sent back by member of class

indicators.note: the head is the top, so just the opening letter of the word
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
sent back means returned, so the whole assembly is read from the end

blocks.note: the cream is the best, the elite
R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, 'take'

explanation.surface: A cook puts a pig's head in cream and the recipe is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: The P goes inside ELITE after the T, R is added, and all of ELITPER is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptiles form the zoological class Reptilia, so any snake or lizard is a member of that class.

clue.text: Crash involving ship in, for instance, conscription service

indicators.note: involving means taking within, so the crash surrounds the rest
in means placed inside, so the ship sits within the example word

blocks.note: prang is British slang for a car crash

explanation.surface: A crash involving a ship, perhaps in the context of conscription.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is British slang for a crash, typically of a car or plane; the two containers nest, the ship within the example and both within the crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang was a band that forcibly enlisted men into the navy, a crude form of compulsory recruitment.

clue.text: Alien retired, retreating from argument

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the joined words are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial withdraws, backing out of a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like a backwards signal but means gone to bed; 'retreating' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion where opposing sides argue their case.

clue.text: Shed takes on mission as a favour

indicators.note: taking on means adding something next, so the second word follows the first

blocks.note: a quest is a mission or search

explanation.surface: The setter Shed accepts an assignment as a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the setter's own pseudonym, so the surface reads as the compiler taking on a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by request means doing it because someone asked, as a kindness to them.

clue.text: Plant from the Eastern Isles

indicators.note: something made from given material is formed out of it, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A plant that grows on islands in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Seseli is a genus of umbelliferous flowering herbs, including moon carrot.

clue.text: Russian ruler with garden tool for Scottish hero

blocks.note: Ivan the Terrible, tsar of Russia
a hoe is a weeding tool

explanation.surface: A tsar with a gardening implement stands in for a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivanhoe is the hero of a novel by the Scottish writer Walter Scott, which is the sense of 'Scottish' here.
explanation.definitionFit: The title knight of Walter Scott's romance is that Scottish author's hero.

clue.text: Snake receiving religious instruction from music maker

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the snake holds the other piece

blocks.note: RI is the school subject abbreviation

explanation.surface: A snake gets a Bible lesson from a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a wooden percussion instrument like a large xylophone, so it makes music.

clue.text: Spy drinking artist's spirits

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the spy swallows the other piece

blocks.note: a mole is a planted spy

explanation.surface: A secret agent knocks back an artist's liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests alcohol after 'drinking', but it means mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and cheerfulness of a person or group, their state of mind.

clue.text: Ban this concoction!

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up from ingredients, so the letters are blended

explanation.surface: A temperance campaigner calls for a prohibition on some drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: absinthe was famously banned in many countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a potent wormwood liqueur that was outlawed in France and elsewhere.

clue.text: Tenant with smaller quantity of drugs

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them

explanation.surface: A renter who has a smaller supply of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, so occupies it as a renter.

clue.text: Where to relax with light music after church

indicators.note: after means following, so the tune comes behind the church

blocks.note: easy as in not heavy, light
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Unwinding to easy-listening music after a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair with padding is the comfortable seat where one sits back and unwinds.

clue.text: Elevenses for publishers' assistant

explanation.surface: Mid-morning refreshment brought for a publishing house's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning break; a cuppa is a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug of tea is the classic British mid-morning snack break drink, so stands for that break.

clue.text: Leaves on equal terms

blocks.note: second meaning: even, with nothing owed either way

explanation.surface: Someone walks away with the score settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons a job walks out; two people who owe each other nothing are even.

clue.text: Someone intellectually challenged to dot Is, perhaps

indicators.note: to dot letters about is to scatter them through a word, so they go inside it

blocks.note: the word itself, read a second time as the host

explanation.surface: Even a slow-witted person can manage to dot their i's.
explanation.walkthrough: Dot is used twice: as the command to scatter, and as the word DOT that the two I's are sprinkled through.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid or foolish person, slow of mind.

clue.text: Cheeky chap on fiddle and piano

blocks.note: P is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A cheeky young man playing violin and piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' and 'piano' look like a pair of instruments, but the fiddle is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a playful rogue.

clue.text: Swiss 18, losing nothing, gets let out

indicators.note: losing something means it drops away, so a letter is removed
let out suggests loosed and scattered, so the letters are set free to rearrange

blocks.note: zero, the letter O, which is removed

explanation.surface: A Swiss version of a Scott hero is released from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Helvetia is the Latin name for Switzerland, hence Helvetian.
explanation.definitionFit: Helvetian is the formal adjective for Switzerland and its people, from the Latin Helvetia.

clue.text: Serious bridge opponents first produce artwork

indicators.note: first means coming at the front, so the opponents are placed before the other word

blocks.note: East and North are opposing partnerships at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Players at a solemn bridge game open by making some art.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut a design into metal or wood, making a printed picture.

clue.text: Shorty goes to Sweden in pain

indicators.note: going to a place means arriving after it, so the shorty follows the country

blocks.note: S is Sweden's international vehicle code
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A short person travels to Sweden and ends up suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp ache in the side, often caused by running.
